name: Australia
summary_text: Australia is exceptionally safe for trans visitors. Gender identity has been a protected ground under the federal Sex Discrimination Act since 2013, and in August 2024 the Federal Court's landmark Tickle v Giggle ruling confirmed that gender-identity discrimination protection covers trans women as women — with compensation awarded. States have modernised rapidly: Queensland strengthened discrimination and vilification protections (April 2024) and NSW passed the Equality Legislation Amendment (LGBTIQA+) Act 2024. There are no bathroom laws and no border friction. Counterweights: the Tickle case itself arose from organised exclusionary activism, which is vocal in Australia; ANROWS documents systemic discrimination and harassment of trans people; and a NSW court granted a trans woman an apprehended-violence order against a Binary Australia activist who had targeted her — real harassment, but also functioning legal recourse. For a visitor: full legal protection and functioning courts; low incident probability.

sources.title: Current and emerging threats to trans and gender diverse human rights: Australian Human Rights Commission - ANROWS - Australia's National Research Organisation for Women's Safety
sources.claim_summary: ANROWS resource: 'Current and emerging threats to trans and gender diverse human rights in Australia' — research-foundation briefing on anti-trans campaigns and rights rollbacks in the context of violence-against-women research.

Queensland Parliamentary Library research brief (2003) 'Protecting Transgender Rights under Queensland's Discrimination Law Amendment Act 2002': introduced 'gender identity' as a protected attribute; documents trans people's difficulties with sex designations on passports, licences and birth certificates, high job-loss rates around transition, and greater exposure to assault and harassment in public places.

sources.title: Intersex is not a gender identity, and the implications for legislation - InterAction
sources.claim_summary: Organisation Intersex International Australia briefing: 'Intersex is not a gender identity' - argues against folding intersex into SOGI legal frameworks, recommends SOGIESC terminology; relevant to how Australian law protects (or fails to protect) intersex and gender-diverse people.

Australian Lesbian & Gay Archives, 'Towards Homosexual Equality in Australian Criminal Law - A Brief History' (Carbery, 2nd ed. 2014): state-by-state history of decriminalisation, from British-inherited buggery laws (death penalty in Victoria until 1949) through reform - historical legal context for Australia's current framework.
